resolved_exit_items.title: Confirm Exact Production Identity Provider (IdP)
resolved_exit_items.resolution: Google Cloud Identity / Google Workspace organizational identity selected as first production IdP.
resolved_exit_items.token_model: Human authentication uses Google OpenID Connect. Google ID tokens are signed JWT identity assertions. OAuth access tokens are separate bearer credentials for calling authorized Google APIs and are not used as the canonical E-7 identity assertion.
resolved_exit_items.verification: Signature validation using keys obtained through dynamic OIDC discovery/JWKS; issuer validation (https://accounts.google.com); audience validation (matched to approved OAuth 2.0 client ID(s) for the E-7 application/client configuration); expiration validation; nonce/replay protection where applicable; hosted-domain validation only where deployment policy restricts access to approved Google Workspace / Cloud Identity domains. JWKS URI is discovered dynamically via provider discovery metadata and is not hardcoded in domain/business logic.
resolved_exit_items.deployment_boundary: Organization-managed Google Workspace / Cloud Identity domain. Exact production organization/domain identifiers remain deployment configuration and MUST NOT be hardcoded in business logic.
resolved_exit_items.secret_boundary: Zero secrets, client secrets, access tokens, refresh tokens, private keys, or production tenant credentials documented or stored.
resolved_exit_items.provider_neutrality: Provider-neutral architecture is strictly preserved. Zero Google-specific fields are introduced into canonical domain entities (no google_user_id or google_tenant_id). Google sub remains stable external subject mapped via provider-neutral external_identity_mapping (provider/issuer, external_subject sub, E-7 principal reference). users.idp_sub is not frozen as a physical schema field; email is not used as canonical identity identifier. hd != canonical E-7 tenant_id. Tenant scope requires E-7 approved organization/tenant mapping and authorization. Service API key remains frozen Phase-1 initial service-authentication baseline; Google Service Accounts / WIF are OPTIONAL_FUTURE_PROVIDER_CAPABILITY.
resolved_exit_items.notes: Previously blocking Phase-0 exit gate under decision D-EXT-01. Formally resolved via project-authorized provider selection. E-7 RBAC / institutional-role mapping is an implementation/configuration follow-up (standard Google OIDC claims do not provide E-7 application roles). Service API key remains initial service-auth mechanism. Technical adapter/configuration implementation timing follows in Phase 1 perimeter authentication foundation sequence.

resolved_exit_items.title: Confirm First Production Calendar System/Provider
resolved_exit_items.resolution: Google Calendar under Google Workspace selected as first production calendar provider with BIDIRECTIONAL integration direction.
resolved_exit_items.sync_reliability_rule: Google Calendar change notifications are an optimization and change signal, not the sole source of synchronization correctness. Notifications do not contain event payloads and Google does not guarantee delivery of every notification. Provider adapter design combines: (1) push notifications to reduce polling latency, (2) incremental synchronization via nextSyncToken as primary delta-retrieval mechanism (with HTTP 410 invalid sync token triggering full re-sync), and (3) optional periodic reconciliation/recovery as an E-7 resilience mechanism. E-7 scheduling remains canonical for E-7-owned scheduling state. Google Calendar remains authoritative for its native external calendar state. Synchronization must preserve the frozen external-ID mapping boundary in calendar_links.
resolved_exit_items.secret_boundary: Zero secrets, client secrets, access tokens, refresh tokens, private keys, or production credentials documented or stored.
resolved_exit_items.provider_neutrality: Provider-neutral architecture is strictly preserved. Zero Google-specific fields are introduced into canonical domain entities (no google_calendar_id). Google Calendar identifiers remain secondary external mappings in calendar_links within app/integrations/ adapter boundary.
resolved_exit_items.notes: Previously blocking Phase-0 exit gate under decision D-EXT-02. Formally resolved via project-authorized provider selection. Technical calendar adapter/synchronization implementation timing belongs to later roadmap phases according to the frozen roadmap.
resolved_exit_items.calendar_authorization_topology: CALENDAR_AUTHORIZATION_TOPOLOGY = TO_BE_CONFIRMED_DURING_IMPLEMENTATION. Valid approaches: delegated per-user OAuth, admin-authorized service account with domain-wide delegation, or another least-privilege model. Domain-wide delegation is not mandatory. Least privilege + admin policy + approved OAuth scopes.
resolved_exit_items.time_handling: UTC_SAFE_TIME_HANDLING: Canonical scheduling instants may be normalized to UTC internally; original provider timezone metadata is preserved when synchronization requires it; Google Calendar all-day event date semantics are preserved; timezone/DST conversions handled explicitly; all-day dates are never converted into arbitrary UTC instants.
resolved_exit_items.idempotency_architecture: E-7 owns synchronization idempotency (operation identity, external event mappings, persisted sync state, version-aware updates). Google Calendar does not provide generic idempotency keys; no Google Calendar idempotency-key API is fabricated.
resolved_exit_items.sync_token_lifecycle: Persist nextSyncToken after initial sync; use for incremental delta queries; persist new nextSyncToken. If Google returns HTTP 410 / invalid sync token, local sync cursor is invalidated and full re-sync is performed to obtain fresh nextSyncToken. Not described as security-token rotation.
resolved_exit_items.push_notification_validation: HTTPS callback endpoint; track issued channel IDs and expected resource IDs; unpredictable X-Goog-Channel-Token verified against expected stored value; X-Goog-Resource-State treated as resource-state metadata, not as authentication; notifications are change signals (do not contain complete event data); retrieve state via API.
